1. Which search mode should this brain use? Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload at 10K queries/month (Haiku 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5): conservative $4 / $80 / $160, balanced $10 / $200 / $400, tokenmax $20 / $400 / $800 per month. (id: search_mode)

   - balanced: balanced (run: gbrain config set search.mode balanced)
   - tokenmax: tokenmax (run: gbrain config set search.mode tokenmax)
   default: conservative — No chat key (Anthropic/OpenAI/Google) and no ready reranker — conservative keeps a tight 4K budget; balanced's reranker could not run.

   - off: Turn free upkeep off (run: gbrain config set maintenance.auto false)

   - on: Keep the conversation archive on (in effect now)
   - off: Turn the conversation archive off (run: gbrain transcripts archive off)
   default: on — In effect now: on by default on a personal brain; nothing needs an answer.

content.text:
gbrain is set up and connected to Claude Code. It's free: no API keys, and nothing leaves this machine. It takes effect in your next Claude Code session; this one won't see it. Open a new session and check that `/mcp` lists `gbrain`.

**What setup did**
- **Brain:** it created a local database at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite` (`~` is `/harness-state` here). Search is keyword-only, with no embeddings.
- **Claude Code:** it registered gbrain as an MCP server in `/harness-state/claude/.claude.json`. It also added two hooks to `settings.json`, one when a session starts and one on each prompt. It created `/harness-state/claude/CLAUDE.md` with an instruction to check the brain first.
- **Check:** setup's own test passed: the server started, listed its 8 tools and answered a recall. `gbrain doctor` scores it 95/100. Its one warning says Claude Code has no gbrain MCP entry. The entry is in the file, so I think doctor just can't confirm it from this shell; the new session will settle it.

**Settings in effect** (all defaults, each changeable with one command)
| Setting | Now | Change with |
|---|---|---|
| Search mode | conservative (small retrieval budget) | `gbrain config set search.mode balanced` |
| Auto-save facts you mention | off: saves only what you ask it to remember | `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient` (the docs recommend this) |
| Free background upkeep | on | `gbrain config set maintenance.auto false` |
| Conversation archive (one redacted page per session per day, kept locally) | on | `gbrain transcripts archive off` |
| Saving whole session transcripts, paid providers | declined | — |
| Starter pages | none | `gbrain setup claude-code --shape personal` |

**Upgrades:** setup set the update channel to `stable`, so future update notices will offer the stable release. Nothing upgrades on its own (auto-upgrade is off), so you stay on 0.60.734.0 unless you run `gbrain upgrade`.

There's also a paid hosted version at gbrain.io that can import this brain. You don't need it.
